subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Unit 2 – Lesson 5: Vocabulary and Grammar – Using technology and comparative adverbs
outcomes: I can name technology actions like upload a photo and download an app.
I can use comparative adverbs like faster and more carefully.
I can compare what I can do with a friend.

tf.s: "Upload a photo" means to put a photo on the internet.
tf.why: Yes! You upload to the internet.

tf.s: The comparative of fast is more fast.
The comparative of well is better.
The comparative of badly is badder.
With adverbs ending in -ly, we use more: more carefully.
The comparative of hard is harder.
"She writes more clear than me" is correct.
tf.why: We say "She writes more clearly than me."

tf.s: The Pass first app helps you prepare for an English exam.
tf.why: Correct! That's the Pass first app.

tf.s: We say "turn off the TV" when we stop it.
tf.why: Yes! Turn off = stop it working.

tf.s: "Download an app" means to delete it.
tf.why: Download means to get it onto your device.

boxes.q: I can run ___ than my brother.
I play tennis ___ than my sister.
Please turn ___ the TV. It's time for bed.
boxes.why: Turn off to stop the TV.

boxes.q: Which app helps you prepare for an English exam?

mcq.q: Which phrase means to put a photo on the internet?
Which list has only irregular comparatives?
mcq.why: well → better and badly → worse are irregular.

mcq.q: Which app helps you learn 20 languages?
mcq.why: The name tells you: Learn Languages.

mcq.q: Which group is all technology actions?
o: go online, search the internet, send a message
go skiing, play hockey, do karate
write a diary, collect cards, make models
mcq.why: These are things we do with technology.

mcq.q: Complete: You can find your way ___ (easily) with the app.

o: She writes more clearly than me.
She writes more clear than me.

mcq.q: "I can play basketball well." What is the best comeback in the game?
o: I can play basketball better than you!
I can play basketball weller than you!
I can play basketball more well than you!
I can play basketball good than you!

mcq.q: Why do we say "more carefully" but "harder"?
o: Carefully ends in -ly, so we use more; hard is short, so we add -er.
mcq.why: Two different rules for two kinds of adverb.

o: He swims more fast than me.
He draws more carefully than me.

mcq.q: You want to find information for a project. Which action do you need?
o: press a button on the printer
